mechanism: loss of STIM1 causes spontaneous STING activation at rest
sentence: Here we found that deficiency in the Ca2+ sensor STIM1 caused spontaneous activation of STING and enhanced expression of type I interferons under resting conditions in mice and a patient suffering from combined immunodeficiency.
justification: Founding STIM1–STING bridge: the SOCE Ca2+ sensor keeps STING silent, so STIM1 loss-of-function (CRAC channelopathy) unleashes type I IFN.

mechanism: co-immunoprecipitation; TM-domain mediated (STIM1 aa 1-249 / STING NTD)
sentence: When co-expressed in HEK293T cells, STIM1 was specifically identified from immunoprecipitates of STING (Fig. 4b).
justification: Direct physical contact between the two anchors of the map, mapped to their ER transmembrane domains.

mechanism: ER retention; STIM1 loss accelerates STING exit to the ERGIC after cGAMP
sentence: To check how interaction with STIM1 influences the function of STING, we monitored the translocation kinetics of STING after treatment of WT or Stim1-/- MEFs with 2',3'-cGAMP and observed faster translocation of STING into the ERGIC in Stim1-/- MEFs than in WT cells (Fig. 5b).
justification: Mechanism of the bridge: STIM1 acts as an ER retention factor controlling STING trafficking, the rate-limiting step of STING activation.

mechanism: dose-dependent suppression of cGAMP-induced IFN-beta reporter
sentence: In cells co-expressing STING and increasing amounts of full length or the N- and C-terminal binding fragments of STIM1, we observed a dose-dependent inhibition of luciferase reporter expression (Fig. 5c).
justification: Gain-of-function evidence in human cells that STIM1 dampens STING signalling, including disease-causing STING (SAVI) variants.

mechanism: STING deficiency augments STIM1 translocation and store-operated Ca2+ entry
sentence: Conversely, we also found that STING deficiency augmented translocation of STIM1 and Ca2+ entry triggered by depletion of ER Ca2+ stores.
justification: Reciprocal arm of the bridge: STING restrains SOCE, so innate immune signalling feeds back on Ca2+ entry.

mechanism: indirect, via STING; increased p-TBK1 in STIM1-deficient cells
sentence: Furthermore, we found enhanced levels of phosphorylated TBK1 and accordingly increased ratio of p-TBK1 vs. total TBK1 in Stim1-/- MEFs, BMDMs and STIM1-/- THP1 cells (Fig. 2e).
justification: Shows the STIM1 brake propagates to the STING kinase TBK1 in human monocytic cells; indirect (through STING).

mechanism: ligand binding; also dissociates the STIM1–STING complex
sentence: We activated STIM1 by treatment with thapsigargin that depletes the ER Ca2+ stores, and activated STING using its ligand, 2',3'-cGAMP.
justification: cGAMP binding is what releases STING from STIM1, linking the second messenger to the Ca2+ sensor complex.
